title: Introduce RAG cold-start warmup quickstart with edge prefetch and wasm preprocessor
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: cold-start latency is a common pain for edge-deployed RAG microservices where first requests trigger model warming and index priming; this quickstart demonstrates an opinionated pattern (edge prefetch + lightweight WASM request preprocessor + adaptive prefix cache) to reduce first-request tail latency without changing server-side runtime. What this PR adds: a new quickstart 'rag-coldstart-warmup' with README, a small TypeScript edge worker example that prefetches likely context, a WASM preprocessor Dockerfile and build scaffold, sample Terraform module to deploy to an edge Lambda/edge VM, a small indexed sample corpus and manifest.yaml, and a GH Actions smoke job that validates end-to-end cold-start latency under controlled conditions. Checklist: [x] Quickstart README with architecture diagram and step-by-step run instructions; [x] Local dev script (scripts/run-local.sh) that runs the quickstart in Docker with sample index; [x] Example prefetch policy (heuristics.json) and adaptive prefix cache config; [x] WASM preprocessor build + simple JS shim demonstrating header-based routing and request normalization; [x] Smoke CI job to verify startup and a simple query baseline. Usage summary: follow README to run locally: cd quickstarts/rag-coldstart-warmup && yarn && make build && ./scripts/run-local.sh --index small; the quickstart launches a light HTTP shim (edge prefetcher), a local mini-indexer, and a Redwood dev-runner configured to use a pinned small model variant; sample queries and expected latency numbers are in README. Implementation notes: the edge worker demonstrates speculative fetch of up to three candidate passages using low-cost metadata heuristics before the first token is requested; the WASM preprocessor normalizes incoming tool-call payloads and enforces a size cap to avoid oversized first requests; the adaptive prefix cache is configured to hold the top-K prefix KV entries per session for 30s by default which reduces warm KV misses for repeated short-lived sessions. CI/QA: GH Actions smoke job 'rag-warmup-smoke' executes a cold-start timeline measurement and fails if 95th percentile first-token latency exceeds 1.2x baseline; unit tests cover the preprocessor and heuristic policy; integration test runs a headless scenario with synthetic traffic. Backwards compatibility: purely opt-in quickstart; server side expects no protocol changes. Related items: reference design doc in DOCS-198 and ENG-3456 for runtime knobs and perf targets; follows patterns in existing quickstarts but emphasizes an edge-first prefetch strategy and a WASM-based preprocessing shim. Migration notes: none for runtime, this is training material and sample configs only. Merge summary and outcome: 6 commits squashed into one merge, all CI green after a single re-run of flaky e2e, merged via squash. Links: internal linear ENG-3456 (https://linear.app/company/ENG-3456) and DOCS-198 (https://linear.app/company/DOCS-198).

release_notes: Add RAG cold-start warmup quickstart demonstrating edge prefetch + WASM preprocessor + adaptive prefix cache; includes sample configs, Terraform edge module, and a smoke CI job for cold-start latency validation.
notes_on_testing: Local validation: run scripts/run-local.sh --index small then run ./scripts/bench-first-token.sh to measure cold-start; CI runs rag-warmup-smoke.yml which measures 95th percentile first-token latency and basic functional assertions.
estimate_runtime: Under 15 minutes to run the quickstart locally on a developer machine with Docker installed.
